text: The nmc_complaints table stores citizen complaints submitted to the Nagpur Municipal Corporation. Each row represents a single civic complaint with fields: complaint_id (UUID primary key), ward_id (the zone such as ZONE-1 through ZONE-10), category (type of complaint such as waterlogging, pothole, garbage, streetlight, drainage), description (free text from the citizen), status (open, in_progress, resolved, closed), source_record_id (the original ID from the citizen app), source_system (the system that ingested it), sensitivity (always restricted because it contains citizen PII), created_at (timestamp), updated_at (timestamp), and event_id (UUID linking back to the ingestion event).

To count NMC complaints by status, query: SELECT status, COUNT(*) as total FROM nmc_complaints GROUP BY status. To filter by a specific ward zone use: WHERE ward_id = 'ZONE-5'. Common statuses are open, in_progress, resolved, closed. The ward_id column uses values like ZONE-1, ZONE-2, up to ZONE-10.

Example questions answerable from nmc_complaints: How many complaints are open in Zone 5? Which ward has the most unresolved complaints? How many waterlogging complaints were filed this week? What is the average time to resolve a pothole complaint? Use created_at for date filtering and status for lifecycle filtering.

The traffic_events table stores traffic incidents and congestion events reported by the city traffic management system. Fields: event_id (UUID primary key), ward_id (zone of the incident), junction (name of the road junction), severity (low, medium, high, critical), event_type (congestion_detected, accident_reported), average_speed_kmph (integer), vehicle_count (integer), camera_id (ID of the traffic camera that reported the event), rain_detected (boolean), source_record_id, occurred_at (timestamp of the event), received_at (when it was ingested).

To analyse traffic congestion use: SELECT junction, AVG(average_speed_kmph) as avg_speed, COUNT(*) as event_count FROM traffic_events WHERE severity = 'high' GROUP BY junction ORDER BY avg_speed ASC. To find accident hotspots: SELECT junction, COUNT(*) FROM traffic_events WHERE event_type = 'accident_reported' GROUP BY junction ORDER BY count DESC.

Example questions answerable from traffic_events: Which junctions have the highest congestion? How many accidents were reported this month? What is the average vehicle speed on Wardha Road? How many events involved rain? Use occurred_at for time-based filtering and severity for priority filtering.

The water_sensor_readings table stores real-time telemetry from water distribution network sensors across Nagpur. Fields: reading_id (UUID primary key), sensor_id (unique identifier like WTR-SENSOR-089), asset_name (name of the feeder line or reservoir), ward_id (zone), pressure_bar (float, current water pressure), flow_lpm (float, flow rate in litres per minute), level_cm (float, water level in centimetres), status (normal, warning, critical), alert_raised (boolean), event_type (sensor_reading, water_alert), occurred_at (timestamp of the reading), received_at (ingestion timestamp).

To check water pressure anomalies: SELECT sensor_id, asset_name, AVG(pressure_bar) as avg_pressure FROM water_sensor_readings WHERE status != 'normal' GROUP BY sensor_id, asset_name ORDER BY avg_pressure. To find sensors with recent alerts: SELECT sensor_id, asset_name, occurred_at FROM water_sensor_readings WHERE alert_raised = true ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 20.

Example questions answerable from water_sensor_readings: Which sensors are currently in warning status? What is the average flow rate on the Gorewada Feeder Line? How many water alerts were raised in the last 24 hours? Which zones have the lowest water pressure? Use occurred_at for time filtering and status or alert_raised for condition filtering.

The health_camp_records table stores data about community health camps organised by the NMC health department. Fields: record_id (UUID primary key), facility_name (name of the camp or community health centre), ward_id (zone), services (array of services offered like general-checkup, vaccination, blood-test), capacity (integer, maximum patients), registered_patients (integer), waiting_patients (integer), average_wait_minutes (integer), camp_status (active, completed, cancelled), event_type (health.camp.status, health.camp.capacity), occurred_at (timestamp), received_at (ingestion timestamp). This table requires role ROLE_HEALTH_OFFICER to access.

To analyse health camp capacity: SELECT facility_name, capacity, registered_patients, ROUND(100.0 * registered_patients / capacity, 1) as utilisation_pct FROM health_camp_records WHERE camp_status = 'active' ORDER BY utilisation_pct DESC. Only users with role ROLE_HEALTH_OFFICER are allowed to query this table.

Example questions answerable from health_camp_records: Which health camps are over 90 percent capacity? What is the average waiting time across active camps? How many patients are currently waiting in Zone 3? Which camp offers vaccination services? Use camp_status = 'active' for current data. Access restricted to ROLE_HEALTH_OFFICER.

The ev_bus_telemetry table stores real-time location and status data from the NMC electric bus fleet. Fields: telemetry_id (UUID primary key), bus_id (unique bus identifier like BUS-EV-021), route_id (route identifier like ROUTE-12), ward_id (current zone), speed_kmph (integer, current speed), battery_soc (integer, state of charge as percentage 0-100), passenger_count (integer), bus_status (in-service, idle, charging, breakdown), event_type (ev.bus.telemetry, ev.bus.breakdown), occurred_at (timestamp), received_at (ingestion timestamp).

To check fleet battery health: SELECT bus_id, route_id, battery_soc, bus_status FROM ev_bus_telemetry ORDER BY occurred_at DESC to get the latest reading per bus, or use: SELECT bus_id, MIN(battery_soc) as min_soc FROM ev_bus_telemetry WHERE occurred_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour' GROUP BY bus_id HAVING MIN(battery_soc) < 20. To find breakdowns: SELECT bus_id, route_id, occurred_at FROM ev_bus_telemetry WHERE event_type = 'ev.bus.breakdown' ORDER BY occurred_at DESC.

Example questions answerable from ev_bus_telemetry: Which buses have battery below 20 percent? How many buses are currently in service on Route 12? What is the average passenger count across all active buses? Which buses have reported a breakdown today? Use occurred_at for time filtering and battery_soc for charge level filtering.

The users table stores all registered system users including officers, admins, and operators. Fields: id (integer primary key, auto-increment), name (full name of the user), username (unique login name), user_id (unique business identifier string), password (argon2 hashed, never select this column), role (the user's role such as admin, ROLE_HEALTH_OFFICER, nmc_officer, traffic_officer, water_officer, transport_officer), created_at (timestamp of account creation). The password column is strictly forbidden from all queries.

To query users safely: SELECT id, name, username, user_id, role, created_at FROM users. Never include the password column. To count users by role: SELECT role, COUNT(*) as total FROM users GROUP BY role. To find recently created accounts: SELECT username, role, created_at FROM users ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10.

Example questions answerable from users: How many users have the admin role? When was a specific officer account created? How many health officers are registered? List all users created in the last 30 days. Always exclude the password column from SELECT statements.

The audit_logs table records every query executed through the query service, providing a full audit trail for compliance. Fields: log_id (UUID primary key), username (who made the query), user_id, role (the role at time of query), sql_query (the SQL that was executed or attempted), status (ALLOWED or BLOCKED), block_reason (why it was blocked if status is BLOCKED), row_count (number of rows returned for ALLOWED queries), timestamp (when the query was executed), ip_address (optional).

To review audit activity: SELECT username, role, status, block_reason, timestamp FROM audit_logs ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 50. To count blocked queries by user: SELECT username, COUNT(*) as blocked_count FROM audit_logs WHERE status = 'BLOCKED' GROUP BY username ORDER BY blocked_count DESC. To find PII access attempts: SELECT username, sql_query, timestamp FROM audit_logs WHERE status = 'BLOCKED' AND block_reason LIKE '%PII%' ORDER BY timestamp DESC.

Example questions answerable from audit_logs: How many queries were blocked this week? Which users have the most blocked queries? What SQL was attempted that triggered a security block? How many queries did each officer run today? Use status = 'ALLOWED' for successful queries and status = 'BLOCKED' for security events.

Cross-department summary query: To get an overview of all civic activity by zone, join the ward_id column that exists in nmc_complaints, traffic_events, water_sensor_readings, and ev_bus_telemetry. Example: SELECT ward_id, COUNT(*) as complaint_count FROM nmc_complaints WHERE status = 'open' GROUP BY ward_id ORDER BY complaint_count DESC to rank zones by open complaints.

Time-based filtering patterns for NagarVault tables. All tables have an occurred_at or created_at timestamp column in UTC. Use these patterns: last 24 hours: WHERE occurred_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'. Last 7 days: WHERE occurred_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'. Today: WHERE DATE(occurred_at) = CURRENT_DATE. This month: WHERE DATE_TRUNC('month', occurred_at) = DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE).

Zone and ward filtering in NagarVault. All department tables have a ward_id column containing values from ZONE-1 through ZONE-10. To filter by zone: WHERE ward_id = 'ZONE-5'. To compare zones: GROUP BY ward_id. Nagpur is divided into 10 administrative zones. Zone 5 covers the central business district. Zone 1 is the northernmost zone.

NMC complaint categories and their SQL filter values. The category column in nmc_complaints uses these string values: waterlogging (flooding and drainage issues), pothole (road surface damage), garbage (waste collection failures), streetlight (broken or missing street lighting), drainage (blocked or overflowing drains). Example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nmc_complaints WHERE category = 'waterlogging' AND status = 'open'.

NMC complaint lifecycle and resolution time analysis. Complaints move through statuses: open -> in_progress -> resolved -> closed. To calculate resolution time: SELECT AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at))/3600) as avg_hours_to_resolve FROM nmc_complaints WHERE status = 'resolved'. To find overdue complaints: SELECT complaint_id, category, ward_id, created_at FROM nmc_complaints WHERE status = 'open' AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'.

Traffic severity levels and event type values. The severity column in traffic_events uses: low (minor slowdown), medium (notable congestion), high (major congestion), critical (road blocked). The event_type column uses: congestion_detected (automatic sensor detection) or accident_reported (manually reported incident). Camera IDs follow the pattern CAM-{ROAD_CODE}-{NUMBER} such as CAM-WR-12 for Wardha Road camera 12.

Water sensor status thresholds. The status column in water_sensor_readings uses: normal (all readings within expected range), warning (pressure below 1.5 bar or flow deviation over 20 percent), critical (pressure below 0.5 bar or flow stopped). The alert_raised boolean is true whenever status is warning or critical. Typical pressure_bar range is 1.5 to 5.0. Typical flow_lpm range is 100 to 800.

EV bus battery and operational status values. The bus_status column in ev_bus_telemetry uses: in-service (bus is on route with passengers), idle (bus is parked and not running a route), charging (bus is at a charging station), breakdown (bus has reported a fault). The battery_soc column is an integer percentage from 0 to 100. Buses are typically recalled for charging when battery_soc drops below 20.

Sensitivity levels in NagarVault data. The sensitivity column is present in the ingestion event but may not appear in the derived tables. NMC complaints are always sensitivity=restricted because they contain citizen name and phone. Traffic, water, and transport data are sensitivity=internal. Health camp data is sensitivity=internal but the table itself has role-based access control for ROLE_HEALTH_OFFICER.

Aggregation and reporting queries for NMC. To build a daily complaint summary report: SELECT DATE(created_at) as day, category, ward_id, COUNT(*) as total, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as resolved FROM nmc_complaints GROUP BY DATE(created_at), category, ward_id ORDER BY day DESC, total DESC.

Aggregation and reporting queries for traffic. To summarise peak congestion hours: SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM occurred_at) as hour, AVG(vehicle_count) as avg_vehicles, AVG(average_speed_kmph) as avg_speed FROM traffic_events GROUP BY EXTRACT(HOUR FROM occurred_at) ORDER BY avg_vehicles DESC.

Aggregation and reporting queries for water. To compute daily average pressure per feeder line: SELECT DATE(occurred_at) as day, asset_name, AVG(pressure_bar) as avg_pressure, AVG(flow_lpm) as avg_flow, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE alert_raised = true) as alert_count FROM water_sensor_readings GROUP BY DATE(occurred_at), asset_name ORDER BY day DESC.

Aggregation and reporting queries for health. To see camp utilisation summary (ROLE_HEALTH_OFFICER only): SELECT ward_id, COUNT(*) as active_camps, SUM(capacity) as total_capacity, SUM(registered_patients) as total_registered, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(registered_patients) / SUM(capacity), 1) as overall_utilisation_pct FROM health_camp_records WHERE camp_status = 'active' GROUP BY ward_id ORDER BY overall_utilisation_pct DESC.

Aggregation and reporting queries for EV bus fleet. To get the current fleet status snapshot: SELECT bus_status, COUNT(*) as bus_count, AVG(battery_soc) as avg_battery, AVG(passenger_count) as avg_passengers FROM ev_bus_telemetry WHERE occurred_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes' GROUP BY bus_status.

PostgreSQL specific syntax reminders for NagarVault queries. Use ILIKE for case-insensitive string matching. Use EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM interval) for duration in seconds. Use DATE_TRUNC for rounding timestamps. Use CURRENT_DATE for today. Use NOW() for current timestamp. All tables use UUID primary keys except users which uses integer id. Boolean columns use true/false not 1/0.

NagarVault data schema overview. There are 7 main tables: nmc_complaints (NMC department civic complaints), traffic_events (traffic and accident data), water_sensor_readings (water network telemetry), health_camp_records (health camp data, restricted access), ev_bus_telemetry (electric bus fleet data), users (system user accounts), audit_logs (query audit trail). All department tables share ward_id (ZONE-1 to ZONE-10) and have timestamp columns for time filtering.

Row count and existence checking patterns. To check if any data exists: SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM nmc_complaints WHERE status = 'open'). To count total rows: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM traffic_events. To get the most recent record: SELECT * FROM water_sensor_readings ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 1. To check last activity: SELECT MAX(occurred_at) as last_event FROM ev_bus_telemetry.

Security rules enforced at the query service level. All queries must be SELECT statements — no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, or other DML/DDL. The following column names are always blocked regardless of table: name, phone, email, address, aadhaar. The health_camp_records table can only be queried by users with role ROLE_HEALTH_OFFICER. Queries violating these rules are rejected before execution and logged to audit_logs with status BLOCKED.

Joining across NagarVault tables. The ward_id column is the natural join key across department tables. Example cross-department query: SELECT n.ward_id, COUNT(DISTINCT n.complaint_id) as open_complaints, COUNT(DISTINCT t.event_id) as traffic_events FROM nmc_complaints n LEFT JOIN traffic_events t ON n.ward_id = t.ward_id AND t.occurred_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours' WHERE n.status = 'open' GROUP BY n.ward_id ORDER BY open_complaints DESC. Note: avoid joining users or audit_logs with department tables in a single query.
